title: Retain single-pass Tropical scalar canonicalizer after tuple-reuse audit

masterplan.active_gate: Gate 1 — Renovation, owner-directed Genesis and general computer assistance

scope: Audit _stored_values Tropical persistence for the concrete case where an already canonical exact tuple of finite non-negative float values is copied through a temporary list and a new tuple. Permit an in-owner tuple-reuse path only if it preserves int-to-float normalization, negative-zero canonicalization, finite/non-negative and semiring-zero refusal, first-error behavior and direct/from_dict constructor semantics without adding a second scalar-validation path, cache, alternate semiring adapter or trusted constructor.

current_owner.finding: Tropical persistence deliberately differs from Boolean, Natural and EvidenceDag: every accepted scalar is normalized to an exact float and signed zero is canonicalized to +0.0. A single bounded pass both validates caller order and builds the canonical immutable value tuple.

candidate_fast_path.finding: Reusing an exact tuple is only sound when every element is already an exact finite non-negative float and no element is -0.0. Determining that fact requires scanning the whole tuple. If any int, signed zero, foreign scalar, infinity, NaN or negative value is encountered, the existing canonicalization/refusal logic must still run in original caller order.

duplicate_validation_cost.finding: A preflight tuple-reuse scan followed by the existing canonicalizer on fallback would duplicate Tropical type/finite/sign predicates and can traverse non-canonical tuples twice. That is a second admission surface inside the same helper for a speculative allocation win with no measured workload evidence.

lazy_copy_alternative.finding: A lazy-copy variant would need extra state to retain the already-validated prefix and would either slice/copy that prefix when normalization first becomes necessary or retain a parallel builder path. This increases code and branch complexity while leaving mutable inputs, integer costs and signed-zero inputs on the allocation path.

semantic_zero_boundary.finding: Tropical additive zero is non-finite positive infinity; persisted relation blocks already refuse non-finite values before storage. Numeric cost 0.0 is a valid multiplicative identity and must remain storable, with -0.0 normalized to +0.0.

audit.gardener_conclusion: Do not add an unmeasured tuple-reuse fast path. Retain the current one-pass Tropical canonicalizer as the single scalar admission/normalization owner. The extra list+tuple materialization is bounded and buys one simple error-ordered implementation; optimization requires a measured allocation hotspot or backend-level evidence first.

semantic_invariants.numeric_contract: Only exact int/float Tropical costs are admitted; bool and foreign numeric-like objects remain refused.
semantic_invariants.normalization: Accepted ints normalize to float, -0.0 canonicalizes to +0.0, and already-positive finite floats retain their numeric value.
semantic_invariants.finite_non_negative: NaN, infinities, negative costs and float-overflowing integers remain refused in caller order.
semantic_invariants.tropical_zero: Semiring additive zero (+inf) remains unpersistable while numeric 0.0 remains a valid persisted multiplicative identity.
semantic_invariants.constructor_boundary: TypedRelationBlock.__post_init__ remains the single persisted scalar-sequence owner for direct, builder and from_dict construction.
semantic_invariants.source_of_truth: KnowledgeForest/Fourfold remain authoritative; relation blocks remain regenerable internal computational views.
semantic_invariants.public_api: No public API, wire schema, benchmark schema, authority or promotion contract changes.

result.summary: GPU-96 rejects a speculative Tropical tuple-reuse preflight because it duplicates scalar admission predicates and makes fallback inputs pay a second traversal without measured hotspot evidence. The existing bounded one-pass list-to-tuple canonicalizer remains the simpler single owner for float normalization, signed-zero canonicalization and refusal precedence.

verification.static_audit: The candidate identity path needs a complete canonicality scan before it can safely return the original tuple. Fallback then either repeats Tropical predicates/conversion or introduces a prefix-copy/builder path. Existing tests already pin int-to-float normalization, negative-zero digest canonicalization, first-error refusal and identity reuse for the non-normalizing semiring families.
verification.reason: No executable behavior changes. Adding a test that Tropical canonical tuples are intentionally copied would overspecify an implementation detail and make a future measured optimization harder without strengthening semantics.
